Hi Casey —

Appreciate the clear ask and the files. We can absolutely present options that balance a price hold with surge protection. High-level framework I propose for Harborline: 

- Option A (Conservative): 12-month fixed price hold at current $/token with a small committed baseline equal to your 90-day trailing average. Surge protection via a 20% escrow bucket (pre-funded) that covers overage at a reduced uplift (e.g., +15% vs list overage). No discount to list, but predictable unit economics.

- Option B (Balanced): 12-month price hold + phased discount ladder tied to a 12‑month commit: 5% discount at 1.1x baseline, 10% at 1.3x, 15% at 1.6x. Surge escrow of 30% of baseline; escrow draws replenish quarterly as usage normalizes.

- Option C (Growth): 18-month term, larger commit (1.5x baseline) with steeper discounts (10/18/25%) and a smaller escrow (15%) with automatic top-up triggers. Includes invoice smoothing (monthly amortization of commit).

Operational notes: 
- We can implement the escrow as a billing credit account that applies to overages automatically once threshold hit.
- For onboarding/ramp we can add a one-time onboarding burst waiver (30% above baseline for first 30 days after go-live) so features that spike usage aren't billed at full overage.

Next steps:
- If any of the options look promising I can run a quick margin check with Finance and return concrete $/token figures and a sample invoice amortization.
- Please confirm whether procurement needs the term to start on 2027-10-01 or whether a September renewal is acceptable.

I'll loop Finance and Ops internally to get exact numbers. Would you be available for a 30‑minute review on Thursday?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Quick pass on numbers based on the usage file and the Option B ladder: baseline = 1.2M tokens/mo (90-day trailing avg). Proposed committed tiers and suggested $/token (net to Redwood) — these are back-of-envelope, Finance will finalize:

- 1.3x baseline (1.56M/mo): 10% discount — net $0.0087/token
- 1.6x baseline (1.92M/mo): 15% discount — net $0.0079/token

Escrow: implement as billing credit account. We can require a 30% pre-fund of baseline (one-time credit of ~360k tokens value) or allow quarterly replenishment. Accounting prefers the pre-funded credit for easier reconciliation; legal prefers a clause that unused escrow credits roll forward for 6 months.

Onboarding burst waiver: ops can configure a 30% waiver for the first 30 days post-renewal but we need a provisioning window of 7 business days to increase capacity for guaranteed throughput. If they want immediate burst on day 1 we can do a temporary soft-cap lift but will require a one-time operational fee.

Marissa — if we go with pre-funded escrow, can you draft the commercial term sheet with the pre-fund option + the quarterly replenish option? Also add a line for a one-time provisioning fee if they request immediate burst on day 1.

Eve — if this looks good I'll run the precise ARR/margin numbers and prep a short appendix for procurement.
